rows.rule: A permit is required before cutting into or replacing pipes, particularly pipes that will be covered by a wall or buried in the ground.
rows.application: If the repair cuts/replaces concealed drainage piping, plan the permit/inspection path before work.

rows.rule: SF Plumbing Code §104.2 "Exempt Work" lists: (1) repair of leaks not requiring cutting into or removing piping; (2) unstopping of traps, sewers, vents or waste pipes not requiring cutting into or removal of traps or piping; (3) replacement, repair or maintenance of faucets, angle stops, hose bibbs or roof drain not requiring cutting into or removal of piping.
rows.application: A seized trip lever that cannot be freed from the overflow opening is not on this list; the exemptions turn on not cutting into or removing piping, which is exactly the condition in dispute here.

rows.rule: DBI lists eligible license classes and limits owner-self-work; registered contractors use PermitSF/AUTH.
rows.application: Confirm the actual permit holder and license class; registration is not verified for any lead.

rows.rule: Plumbing/mechanical work must be inspected before pipes are covered; remodel final inspection waits for trade finals.
rows.application: Keep the cavity open until required sign-off.

rows.rule: BPC §7057 allows a B prime contract for other trades when it requires at least two unrelated trades, or the B holds the appropriate classification/subcontracts appropriately.
rows.application: Name the plumbing and restoration parties; do not infer drywall self-performance from B + C-36 alone.

rows.rule: B-2 requires at least three unrelated trades on existing residential wood-frame work and restricts structural work and plumbing-system installation/replacement/substantial alteration.
rows.application: HARP/24-7 #1105133 is not an automatic two-trade plumbing-plus-drywall fit.

rows.rule: BPC §7048 (effective 2026-01-01) has a conditional under-$1,000 aggregate exemption; it does not apply when a building permit is required, for larger operations, or to persons advertising as contractors/employing others.
rows.application: The supplied quote amounts do not establish an exemption; confirm permit status and aggregate scope.

rows.rule: Civil Code §1954 permits necessary/agreed repairs during normal business hours with reasonable written notice; 24 hours is presumed reasonable, mailed notice six days.
rows.application: Document notice, hours and any consent/exception for each affected tenancy.

rows.rule: CSLB requires a written contract over $500; down payment is no more than the lesser of 10% or $1,000, with a rare blanket-bond exception; change orders are written.
rows.application: Put scope, permits, cleanup, schedule, price, warranty and payment terms in writing.

rows.rule: EPA RRP requires certified firms/trained lead-safe practices for paid paint-disturbing work in pre-1978 rentals.
rows.application: Building age is unknown; screen before disturbing paint and leave applicability unconfirmed until assessed.

rows.rule: EPA advises leaving suspect material alone and using trained/accredited professionals for sampling or disturbance.
rows.application: Conditional screening control; no asbestos finding is made.

rows.rule: July 2026 DBI Table 1A-C lists Category 1P at $290, with separate inspection/reinspection rates.
rows.application: Fee category and total project cost are unconfirmed; fees are not contractor quotes.

rows.rule: SF Plumbing Code §104.5 provides that "the replacement of a plumbing fixture or a gas appliance without a change in drainage, piping or venting shall not require the payment of permit issuance fee."
rows.application: Relevant only if the scope is a like-for-like fixture change with no drainage or piping change. A stuck assembly behind the wall is unlikely to meet that condition, and the fee waiver is not a permit exemption.

rows.rule: SF.gov states that contractors with only a B licence get electrical and plumbing permits right away only when those permits are directly associated with a kitchen or bath permit; otherwise plumbing scope is approved based on the scope of work.
rows.application: A standalone overflow repair is not a kitchen or bath remodel permit, so a B-only lead may need the C-36 party or written DBI approval to be permit holder.
